sender.name: Vellynne Harpell
sender.title: Personal Journal of Vellynne Harpell
sender.subtitle: Tenth Black Staff of Blackstaff Academy

metadata.deliveryMethod: Written by candlelight in my quarters at the Northlook Inn

paragraphs.text: Three days have passed since the party departed with their Illithid ally, and the silence from the sending stone grows more ominous by the hour. I've attempted contact no fewer than seven times—each attempt met with that peculiar emptiness that suggests the recipients are either dead, in another plane entirely, or somewhere magic simply cannot reach.

The latter possibility disturbs me most. Few places in this material plane can completely sever magical communication, and most of them are locations no sane person would venture willingly. Yet knowing Rothbart's insufferable sense of duty and his companions' talent for stumbling into impossibly dangerous situations, I suspect they've managed exactly that.

My scrying attempts have yielded equally frustrating results. The waters show me only swirling mists and shadows—a sure sign of powerful magical interference or planar displacement. I've exhausted three different scrying focuses, each more expensive than the last, with nothing to show for it but a growing certainty that standard divination magics will not locate them.

The political situation in Bryn Shander continues to deteriorate in their absence. Duvessa maintains her composure publicly, but I've observed her checking the sending stone with increasing frequency. Naerth grows bolder by the day, making subtle inquiries about "contingency plans" should our heroes fail to return. The man's opportunism knows no bounds—though I admit a grudging respect for his timing.

More troubling are the reports filtering in from the North Watch. Increased undead activity near the Reghed Glacier, strange lights in the sky where none should be, and two separate accounts of "star-filled holes" appearing and disappearing in the wilderness. The ranger who reported the last claim was stone sober and had no history of flights of fancy. Something significant is stirring in the wasteland beyond the Ten Towns.

I've been analyzing the fragments of intelligence they gathered before departure. The Netherese spire they sought was reportedly protected by illusions that could fool even Illithid perception—a feat that should be impossible given the mental acuity of their kind. If such protections exist, they represent magic far beyond anything I've encountered in my studies of the fallen empire.

The irony is not lost on me that the vampiric paladin I've spent months needling about his nature may now be the Ten Towns' best hope for survival. His party's unique combination of divine power, arcane knowledge, and sheer stubborn determination has proven remarkably effective against threats that would devastate conventional forces. Their absence creates a void that no amount of political maneuvering or strategic planning can fill.

I find myself in the unusual position of genuinely hoping for their safe return—not merely for the advancement of my research or the completion of our bargains, but because they've proven themselves worthy allies in ways I hadn't anticipated. The dampir's moral consistency, while occasionally tiresome, provides a stabilizing influence I've come to appreciate. Even his sanctimonious tendencies serve their purpose in these increasingly desperate times.

If they have indeed found passage to Ythryn or become trapped in some Netherese dimensional pocket, the implications extend far beyond their personal safety. The knowledge they might gain—or the threats they might unleash—could reshape the very fabric of Icewind Dale's future. Ancient Netherese sites are notorious for their unpredictable temporal and spatial distortions. They could emerge tomorrow, a century hence, or never at all.

I've begun preparing for multiple contingencies. Should they return bearing knowledge of Ythryn's location, I must be ready to act swiftly. Should they fail to return at all, I must adapt my research methods and perhaps consider more... aggressive approaches to accessing the fallen city. The Brotherhood's patience with my northern expedition grows thin, and I cannot afford to return to Waterdeep empty-handed.

For now, I continue my vigil. The sending stone remains within arm's reach, charged and ready. I've instructed the inn's staff to wake me immediately should any word arrive, regardless of the hour. Whether they return as heroes bearing ancient wisdom or as refugees fleeing unspeakable horrors, I suspect their next appearance in Bryn Shander will herald significant changes for everyone involved.

The stars tonight seem unusually bright for Icewind Dale. I choose to interpret this as a favorable omen, though my scholarly training warns against such superstitions. Sometimes, however, hope proves more valuable than empirical observation.

content.postscript: Must remember to acquire more high-quality parchment. This northern climate wreaks havoc on proper writing materials. Also, the inn's ale grows more tolerable with each passing day—a concerning development that bears monitoring.
